cells.remarks: Refers to the grant of a village called Chandrabhāṇupura by Madaken-Nāyaka, son of Mahānāyaka Kastūri Bara-manna-Nāyaka, on which occasion the right of worship in the temple of Hanumanta at that place, granted by a certain Ranga-chārya, the priest of the village, was given to him, while the Nāyaka granted. cells.date: Śaka 612, Siddhārthin, Māgha, śu. di. trayodaśī, Monday.
cells.remarks: Incomplete. Registers the gift of the village Kuṇeduru on the bank of the Tuṅgabhadra by the king on the occasion of the installation of his two sons, Yuvarāja Vikramāditya-Kumāravinaya and Tānu-Choḍa and Shanmukha-Choḍa as yuvarājas. The village was divided into four shares two of which were given to the gods Agastyēśvara and Mahādēva and Kumārasvāmin at Tānu-maṇḍala. The third share was given to his own purōhit and the fourth to the worshippers, servants, &c., of the two temples.

cells.king: Śaribha-Choḍadēva of the Koḍa family, residing at Nellūrapuṭi.
cells.remarks: These are the missing third and fourth plates of No. 24 of Appendix A to the Annual Report for 1914-15, which makes that grant complete. Registers the grant with all the privileges of the village Marrigunḍi sarramad Raghunāthapuram situated in the Valanāḍu division of the Roṇḍavēṭa-sīma to the great scholar and astronomer Sarva-Bhaṭṭa, who belonged to the Āpastamba-sūtra, Bhāradvāja-gōtra and was a Yajurvēdin. He was the son of Koṇḍu-Bhaṭṭa and grandson of Sarva-Bhaṭṭa and was a resident of the village Pennumpaḷi as also a devotee of the god Gōpīnāthadēva. The gift was made on the representation of the king's minister Rāma-rāja.

cells.remarks: Records the grant of the village Kōmyana in the Vōda-vishaya with all its income to the Dīkshita Jagadharaśarman, of the village Padhuvādapāku in the Kōntavēṅga-vishaya. The donee belonged to the Bhāradvāja-gōtra and Mādhyandina-śākhā and was a student of the Yajur-vēda. He was well-versed in the Śrauta and Smārta rites and was strong in astronomy (jyōtiḥ-śāstra). The grant was made on the uchchāyana-ēkādaśī day in the bright half of the Kārtika month when Vishnu is believed to wake up from his four-months' sleep.

cells.date: Saka 1002 Durmati, Vaisakha, su. di. tritiya.
cells.remarks: States that, while Liṅgōji-Paṇḍita was governing the Karṇāṭaka kingdom from Peṇugonda-paṭṭaṇa as a subordinate of Akhammā-dēvi, the younger sister of the king, Mallanna-Paṇḍita who was the head of Brāhmaṇas and the chief officer of the king of Bhāganagar, Nāyappa of the Kāmakhāyana-Viśvāmitra-gōtra, Āśvalāyana-sūtra and Rik-śākhā who was the sthala-karṇam of Lēpākshi in the Kōṇḍapi-nāḍu in Paṇugonḍa-rājya gave some land in Lēpākshi to the temple of the Bhāradvāja-gōtra, Āpastamba-sūtra and Yajud-śākhā, who was the arādhyan at Lēpākshi. It registers also the gift of rates on puck-bullocks, shops, looms and morringas to the samo Kumārayya by the ayyāvas of Ayyāvali, etc., the Vaisya of the 18 gōtras of the Penugonda-paṭṭaṇa and of the Yajamānas of the Lēpākshi-sthala etc., assembled in the temple mandapa of that place for daily offerings and lamps to the god Nañjuṇḍēśvara.

cells.remarks: States that a certain Pedda Aholalēndri who was a divan under Mahāmaṇḍalēśvara Kṛishṇadēvarāya who was ruling at Peṇugonda, gave some land to Aholalam at Peṇu-Lakshmi Nrisimhasvāmin at -omaghaṭṭa in accordance with the direction given to him by the deity at Ahōbalam in a dream. cells.remarks: The Saka date falls into the reign of Virupaksha I predecessor of Bukka II. Registers in detail the incomes that the guarding officers (kaval-doregalu) of Madakaira were to get from the several classes of people, residing in the village. Also specifies the incomes that the ayagaras (i.e., the village servants) of certain villages were to get after the king's share was deducted.

cells.date: Śaka 1488, 28th year, Mahara 16, Wednesday, [29], Śukla-di-ēkādaśī, Moudhy-bha-karyōga, Śu-bhaya. [date-calculation appendix, No. 619: Śaka 1478, 6th year, Naḷa, Varsha-ritu, [Maka] ra 29, śu. di. ēkādaśī, Monday, Pushya. In A.D. 1557 Naḷa, Pushya combined with Monday on only two occasions :- (i) Simha 4, ba. trayōdaśī (August 3) and (2) Kanya 1, ba. dvādaśī (August 31). Makara 29 was Monday, ba. ēkādaśī but the nakshatra was (not Pushya) Jyēshṭha. It corresponded to A.D. 1556 January 25. cells.date: Śaka 1744, Chitrabhānu, Mārgaśira, śu. di. 10, Monday. [date-calculation appendix, No. 693: Saka 1474, Paridhāvi, Pushya, ba. di., 30, Solar eclipse = A.D. 1553, January 14, Saturday. There was a solar eclipse on Saturday.]
cells.remarks: Relates that Basavalingayya, son of Marayya and Bāramma, the shareholder of a moiety in the mānya-lands of the mathas, Peḍḍgōmatha and Doṇipāḍi and other villages, repaired by raising alms the temple of Vīrabhadrasvāmin at Kōvelakuṇṭla which was in ruins. The merchant classes, on being approached, gave for worship and offering 4 chiṭṭedu of rice and one ruvva-weight of lamp-oil. And on Friday fairs, those who sold by scale, set apart 1 gavaḍi (?) and those who sold by measure, one chiṭṭedu, evidently for the same purpose.

cells.remarks: Helps to the manifestation of the god Ramachandradeva before the 'Eleven Rudras' and to his having received worship at the hand of Cholayya. Registers the construction of the gopuras and the front-mandapas, the several repairs and the performance of sacrifices by Rayaparaja, the grandson of that Chola. He also granted to the god Ramachandra the villages, Ramachandrapura, Isvarapura, Rayasagara, Komudavalli, Sivalinga, in Moligai-simai, in Edadnad, in the Kolar-sima and lands near the tanks of Agali, Maduvidu, Havidu, Kantavalu and Kahi.

cells.location: Śrīkaṇthapuram
cells.place: On a slab set up near the chāvaḍi
cells.date: Śaka 1424, Krō-dhana, Chaitra, śu. di. 1, Wed-nesday. Śaka 969, śrāhe. [date-calculation appendix, No. 757: Śaka 1426, Krōdhana (= Ś. 1427) Chaitra, śn. di. 1, Wednesday. Śaka 1426 (= A.D. 1504-05) corresponded to Rakshasa (not to Krōdhana) in which Chaitra śu. 1 was Sunday. In Krōdhana (= Śaka 1427) Chaitra śu. 1, was Thursday the tithi ending at 91 but Quaitra śu 1, in Śaka 1428 (i.e.,) Kshaya Samvat was Wednesday (= A.D. 1506, March 27, Wednesday). The inscription refers to Chaitra at the beginning or Chaitra at the end of a year. Śaka 1426 (= Krōdhana = A.D. 1505-06), which would be the same as Chaitra at the beginning of A.D. 1506-07 (= Ś. 1428 = Kshaya Samvat).]
cells.remarks: (Erhanganged). Seems to record the grant of the village (Śrīrangasamudra, to a certain Narasimha-Dīkshita of the Ārvalayans-sūtra and the Kāsypana-gōtra.

The lands were variously situated in Edirili-śōḷanallūr, a hamlet of Muḍigoṇḍaśōḷa-chaturvēdimaṅgalam in Māra-nāḍu, a subdivision of Virudarājabhayan-kara-vaḷanāḍu, to the temple of Ānaipayanallūr and Saṅgukkal alias Vikramaśōḷanallūr. Registers that as the existing dēvadāna lands of the temple of Tirumuḍugam-Uḍaiyār were inadequate for meeting the expenses of the temple, lands in lieu thereof for feeding the Mahēśvaras in the Vikramaśōḷa-maṭha, built in the temple were, at the instance of Sōḷakōn, given free of taxes in the village Sōḷa-kūṟṟam-hiṇṭamaṅgalam in Paravūr-kūṟṟam in Iruṅgōḷap-pāḍi. These lands formed into a village named Vikramaśōḷanallūr.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the Mallikārjunasvāmin temple in Kuruvatti. †
cells.date: Ch. Vik. 29, Tāraṇa, Vaiśākha, śu. tadige, Sunday.
cells.remarks: States that the mahājanas of the agrahāra Gaṇḍarādityana-Hoḷaḷ, having complained to the emperor (chakravartti) that Māyidēva, son of the late Hēgāḍe Būchimayya was plundering all properties of the said Hēgāḍe and his family, had the emperor sent for Boppayya, chastised him and took from him an undertaking that he and his successors should secede from the government of Hoḷaḷu. The chief did accordingly in the presence of the thirty-two thousand (representatives) of Beṇṇevūru 12, Niruṅguṇḍa 2, Baḍah-guḷi, Māṅgoḷa, Bidirahaḷḷi, Hābanūru, Honnavatti, Kuru-vaṭṭi and Mūguḷi and drank water at the temple of Tripurāntakadēva.

NOTE.—It is note worthy that these epigraphs, as proved by their dates, should belong to the reign of Kulōttunga-Chōla II whose dated inscription, have so far occurred only in Telugu districts (vide the article on this reign by the present writer in Epigraphia Indica, Vol. XI, page 287). There are no dates satisfying the given details in the reign of either Kulōttunga-Chōla I or Kulōttunga-Chōla III. The blank in No. 380 of 1918, which has been read conjecturally as "bahula" should be "sukla," while "pūrvapaksha" or "śu. di." in No. 528 of 1918, which is quite clear in the impression, is clearly an error for "apurapaksha" or "ba. di.," the combination of śu. 9 and nak. "Visakha" in Makara mouth not being possible except in aparapaksha. See the present writer's Eye-table.]

text.date: 10th year, Makara, śu. di. Navami, Monday, Viśākha. [date-calculation appendix, No. 528: 10th year, Makara, śu. di. 9, Monday, Visakha. = Monday, 11th January A.D. 1143; .62; .42. NOTE.—It is note worthy that these epigraphs, as proved by their dates, should belong to the reign of Kulōttunga-Chōla II whose dated inscription, have so far occurred only in Telugu districts (vide the article on this reign by the present writer in Epigraphia Indica, Vol. XI, page 287). There are no dates satisfying the given details in the reign of either Kulōttunga-Chōla I or Kulōttunga-Chōla III. The blank in No. 380 of 1918, which has been read conjecturally as "bahula" should be "sukla," while "pūrvapaksha" or "śu. di." in No. 528 of 1918, which is quite clear in the impression, is clearly an error for "apurapaksha" or "ba. di.," the combination of śu. 9 and nak. "Visakha" in Makara mouth not being possible except in aparapaksha. See the present writer's Eye-table.]

cells.remarks: Registers that a certain Varada-Ramadāsu of Kaḷichi-nagara, who was an incarnation of Śrī-Rāmadāsu of the time of Tanisha, came to Bhadrāchalam and spent his time there as a devotee. He constructed the temple and performed the daily worship of the Haṣanachā-Paragu (in His Exalted Highness the Nizam's State) in the time of Nawab Nāsiruddauḷa and conferred a large part of the income of that Paragana on the temple and the Brahmins who were connected with it. Numerous other details concerning the establishment, festivals, worship, oblations, etc., of the temple are also registered.

cells.location: ANANTAPUR DISTRICT / GOOTY TALUK · Amritalur — Andhra Pradesh
cells.place: On a rough stone set up in a street
cells.remarks: Registers the agreement (Kaula) granted by Mahāmaṇḍalē- śvara Chinna-Timma-Rāja to the people that the settlement at the Amrita (market village) built by him to the south of Amritalur in the name of Mahāmandirāja. No taxes were payable by the settlers in the pēṭa for the first three years. After that period they were required to pay taxes on ploughs, looms, and houses, big and small. States that Nāgappa-Nāyaka the agent (karyakarta) of the King gave an agreement to the merchants, weavers, etc., of Siripuram to pay for three years, taxes on account of a plunder suffered by the people. Refers to Śrīraṅgapaṭaya who was evidently ruling then.

cells.place: On the southern side of the eastern gateway of the Choḍeśvarasvāmin temple. †
cells.remarks: Defines in a ślōka the length of the linear measures of aṅgula, vitasti and daṇḍa and states the circumference of the thumb in an aṅgula. Twelve aṅgulas make one vitasti and thirty-two vitastis make one daṇḍa. In the Telugu portion the kesaripāṭi-ghaḍa which corresponds to the daṇḍa is mentioned. A vertical line is cut over the inscription to give the exact measurement, evidently, of the vitasti. It measures a little over 1 foot and 3 inches.

cells.date: Śaka 1411, Saumya, Vaiśākha, Śukla-paksha, Haridina (i.e. ēkādaśī).
cells.remarks: Damaged. Gives a descriptive praise of the (god) Gōvardhanēśa, who appeared in the form of a cowherd to his devotee Vallabha, quoting the famous verse in the Bhagavad-Gītā, which ends with "Dharmasaṁsthāpanāya sambhavāmi yuge yuge". Says also that the god became manifest (i.e., was installed) and was named Gōvardhanēśa. No date quoted. The Vijayanagara king Kṛishṇarāya and his minister Sāḷuva Timmaraśu are said to have visited the temple and made gifts to it.
